2019 Q1.gq: We are raising guidance for a contract drilling services revenues in 2019 with the new range at $1.04 billion to $1.07 billion, up from the previous range of $1 billion to $1.03 billion.
2019 Q1.bq: Also contract drilling services revenues finished the quarter at the high end of our guided range, while the Company delivered another quarter of excellent operational performance as demonstrated by fleet uptime of 97.8%, which remain near record levels.

2019 Q2.gq: DD&A guidance for 2019 is unchanged at a range of $445 million to $460 million.
2019 Q2.bq: Second quarter revenues were 6% better than our guided range at $255 million to $265 million due primarily to the postponement of scheduled downtime for regulatory inspections on the jackup Noble Scott Marks and Noble Roger Lewis, which will now be completed in the third quarter.

2019 Q3.gq: DD&A guidance for 2019 as being lower to a range of $439 million to $444 million compared to a previous range of $445 million to $460 million..
2019 Q3.bq: Contract drilling services revenues were slightly better than our guided range of $245 million to $255 million due primarily to the Noble Don Taylor and the Noble Sam Croft remaining under contract for a longer than expected period in the quarter before commencing preparations for the relocation to new regions.

2019 Q4.gq: For the first quarter 2020, contract drilling services revenue is expected to range between $260 million and 270 million, nearly in line with fourth quarter adjusted revenue of $274 million.
2019 Q4.bq: Fourth quarter adjusted contract drilling services revenue came in 10% ahead of the midpoint of our guided range of $245 million to $255 million.

2026 Q3.bq: Revenue was narrowed around the high end of the previous range, driven by higher reimbursable revenue than previously expected, while Adjusted EBITDA was narrowed around the lower end, driven primarily by slightly later starts for the Voyager and the Valiant.
